why: Source: four per-capita multiplications plus one comparison (5 steps); question: the same four multiplications of rolls by roll length plus one comparison (5 steps), with only the numbers changed.

Source: contact shares by employer size, an overall contact sum against the total, an uncontacted-pool comparison and a no-data check (about 5 steps); question: the same four statements tested against the same kind of 9x3 table (about 5 steps), only the true statement moves from B to A.

Source: read margins off gridlines, find the highest, test a 4x ratio and reject two absolute-value statements needing market size (about 4 steps); question: read off gridlines, find the highest, test a twice ratio and reject two absolute statements (about 4 steps).

Source: read two cumulative bars off gridlines, subtract, multiply by the total, avoiding the bar-height trap (4 steps); question: the same two readings, subtraction, multiplication and trap (4 steps).

Source: read both index lines, compare the end-point changes, compute revenue times margin index for one month against the base, reject a no-data statement (about 4 steps); question: the same readings, end-point comparison, revenue-times-margin check for July and no-data rejection (about 4 steps).
Source: five ratios of labelled bars from two charts and one ranking (6 steps); question: five income-over-maintenance ratios from two labelled charts and one ranking (6 steps).

Source: total cost from fixed plus attendances times variable cost, subtract neighbouring cumulative bars, multiply (about 4 steps with the cumulative trap); question: identical structure with consultations instead of attendances (about 4 steps).

Source: test four statements, a 20-year extrapolation, a growth comparison with the rest of the market, a growth-pace comparison and a share check (about 4-5 steps); question: the same four statement types on a same-shaped table (about 4-5 steps).

Source: three per-unit share ratios plus two combined-class ratios and four statement checks (about 6 steps); question: the same three per-garage ratios, two combined ratios and four checks (about 6 steps).

Source: pick the right two pies, add percentages for each rating, compare, recognising the same respondents allow adding (about 4 steps); question: the same pie selection, additions and comparison (about 4 steps).
